literature_records.title: Universe-Life-Civilization 5-18-26
literature_records.abstract: This book develops the Lao-Yang Genesis Cosmology (老-杨创世纪宇宙观) — a unified scientific-philosophical framework that integrates Laozi's two foundational propositions from the Dao De Jing with the findings of modern cosmology, thermodynamics, evolutionary biology, systems science, and governance theory. The two propositions are: the 13-character hierarchical principle of Chapter 25 — 人法地，地法天，天法道，道法自 然(Humans follow Earth; Earth follows Heaven; Heaven follows Dao; Dao follows Nature) — and the 13-character generative sequence of Chapter 42 — 道生一，一生二，二生三， 三生萬物 (Dao generates One; One generates Two; Two generates Three; Three generates All Things). Together they constitute the 26-character minimal expression of cosmic cognition: a compact statement of both the hierarchical regulatory structure within which civilisation is embedded and the generative sequence through which that structure came into being. The book demonstrates that these classical Daoist formulations are not merely moral or metaphysical metaphors but correspond to a coherent cosmological order grounded in natural law, self-organisation, and systemic interdependence. The nested generative chain is reconstructed in full scientific detail: the Dao manifested as the self-organising dynamics of the Milky Way; the Milky Way giving rise to the Solar System (One); the Solar System giving rise to Earth (Two); Earth giving rise to the Moon (Three); and the stable Sun–Earth–Moon triadic system generating the conditions for water, air, life, and ultimately human civilisation (All Things). Each step is analysed through the dual lens of modern planetary science and Natural Cybernetics — the author's extension of Wiener's cybernetics and Prigogine's dissipative structure theory to cosmic and civilisational scale. From this cosmological foundation the book derives a comprehensive theory of civilisational governance: Natural Civilisation (自然文明), a governance paradigm in which institutional, economic, and cultural systems are designed to align with rather than override the natural regulatory dynamics that have maintained cosmic and ecological order for 13.8 billion years. The theory diagnoses the contemporary civilisational crisis as civilisational entropy increase — the compound consequence of three interlocking positive feedback loops (the Greed-Technology-Power loop, the Ecological Destruction loop, and the Institutional Failure loop) — and identifies three critical tipping points (Natural, Social, and Technological) whose interaction defines the governance challenge of the twenty-first century. Against this diagnosis, the book proposes the Lao-Yang Hierarchical Governance Framework, operationalising the 人法地法天法道法自然 principle as a four-level governance architecture from local ecological management to global coordination. The book concludes with the theory of Artificial Wisdom (AW) — a paradigm shift in the design of artificial intelligence systems from desire-amplifying optimisers to wisdom- governance systems aligned with Natural Cybernetics principles. Five design principles distinguish AW from current AI: cosmic alignment, negative feedback priority, polycentric architecture, temporal depth, and epistemic humility. The AW framework is proposed as the technological infrastructure of Natural Civilisation and the mechanism through which the Fourth Intellectual Revolution — the application of cosmological, evolutionary, and ecological insights to the governance frameworks of civilisation itself — can be realised in practice. The book synthesises more than a dozen prior publications archived on PhilArchive into the first comprehensive, book-length statement of the Lao-Yang Genesis Cosmology and its implications for the future of human civilisation.

literature_records.title: Fundamental constants: from measurement to the universe, a window on gravitation and cosmology
literature_records.abstract: Abstract Fundamental constants are a cornerstone of our physical laws. Any constant varying in space and/or time would signal a violation of local position invariance and be associated with a violation of the universality of free fall, and hence of the weak equivalence principle at the heart of the geometrisation of gravity. It will also reflect the existence of new degrees of freedom that couple to standard matter fields. Thus, testing for the stability of fundamental constants is of utmost importance for our understanding of gravity and for characterizing the domain of validity of general relativity. Besides, it opens an independent window on the dark matter and dark energy components. As a consequence, thanks to the active developments of experiments, fundamental constants have become a key player in our search for physics beyond the standard model of particle physics and general relativity. This review details the various roles of the fundamental constants in the laws of physics and in the construction of the international system of units, which now depends strongly on them. This requires to distinguish the concepts of fundamental units and fundamental parameters . Then, the relations between constants, the tests of the local position invariance and of the universality of free fall are presented, as well as the construction of field theories that account for “varying constants” and the motivations arising from high-energy physics and string theory. From a theoretical perspective any varying fundamental parameter is related to a dynamical field, the dynamics of which is dictated from the whole theory so that it remains fully consistent: no arbitrary law of variation has to be postulated. Then, the main experimental and observational constraints that have been obtained from atomic clocks, the Oklo phenomenon, solar system observations, meteorite dating, quasar absorption spectra, stellar physics, pulsar timing, the cosmic microwave background and Big Bang nucleosynthesis are described. It details the basics of each system, its dependence with respect to the primary parameters the variation of which can be constrained from observations, the known systematic effects and the most recent constraints. It also describes how these primary parameters can be related to the fundamental constants and the model-dependencies that is involved. Both time and space variations are considered. To finish, it contains a short discussion on the more speculative possibility of understanding the numerical values of the fundamental parameters in view of the apparent fine-tuning that they confront us with, by invoking anthropic arguments. Given the huge increase of data and constraints and the difficulty to standardize them, a general scheme to present experimental and observational results and to construct a collaborative data base that will be more efficient for the community and allow us for better traceability, is proposed.

literature_records.title: Formalisation of Haag-Kastler nets in higher-order logic
literature_records.abstract: This thesis presents formalisations ranging from differential geometry and Lie groups, to abstract treatments of operator algebras and a starting point for a mechanised theory of particle physics. The work is carried out within the simple type theory of Isabelle/HOL, which is less expressive than dependently typed systems, and so one aim of the present work is to review the use of various solutions and tools to allow the formalisation of advanced mathematical concepts in this environment. Our first contribution is a formal theory of Lie groups, which are smooth manifolds with multiplicative structure. Through developing a theory of vector fields on manifolds, the Lie algebra of a Lie group is constructed. Some models of this theory are described, notably the general linear group. The Poincaré group, which appears as a global symmetry group in physics, is constructed as a subgroup of the general linear group. Our second contribution is an early investigation of formalising algebraic quantum field theory (AQFT), a candidate for an axiomatic foundation for particle physics. Specifically, we discuss the definition of Haag-Kastler nets, the fundamental structure of AQFT, as well as required formalisations in several related topics. In particular, an abstract approach to algebras of operators on complex vector spaces is implemented, and concrete representations for all such algebras are obtained by performing the GNS construction as a succession of type quotients and operator extensions. Throughout the thesis, relationships between Isabelle's locales and sets, types and classes are emphasised. We also comment frequently on the use of tools to leverage a certain representational freedom, most notably the transfer mechanism, and the Types-to-Sets framework.

literature_records.title: The universe during epochs of accelerating expansion
literature_records.abstract: Cosmic inflation, the accelerated expansion of the early Universe, is an accepted pillar in the foundations of modern cosmology. This is due mainly to its success at explaining several anomalies between observations and the existing Hot Big Bang model of the Universe, but a specific model is not agreed upon in the literature. The Universe has also recently been observed to enter another phase of accelerating expansion, driven by an unexplained mechanism called ‘dark energy’. The research presented in this thesis grows organically; starting with an investigation into novel inflationary models and developing into quintessential inflation models. The latter explain both the primordial inflation and dark energy observations using one minimal framework. A new family of inflation models is presented, which excellently match observations for natural parameter values, and a derivation from supergravity is demonstrated. A period of thermal inflation allows the supergravity realisation of hybrid inflation to be realigned with observations. A new approach to inflection-point inflation is developed, which is considerably less fine-tuned and exotic than previous models. Two novel quintessential inflation models are introduced, the first embedded in α-attractors - a compelling framework of inflationary model building and the second in Gauss-Bonnet gravity - an extension to General Relativity. Detailed investigations of reheating after inflation are undertaken, focusing on gravitational reheating and instant preheating, analysing the necessary constraints including those from supergravity. Along the way, there is a brief diversion into primordial black holes, investigating how a slow reheating period affects their formation rates.

**A. Executive Finding**  
Early‑universe model building can be organised around three *required* ingredients that appear across the retrieved literature:

| Ingredient | What the sources require | Typical mathematical expression |
|------------|--------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Dynamical law** | A covariant action (or Hamiltonian) governing the metric \(g_{\mu\nu}\) and any additional fields (scalar, vector, gauge, or operator‑algebraic nets). | \(S=\int d^{4}x\sqrt{-g}\,\Big[ \frac{M_{\!P}^{2}}{2}R +\mathcal{L}_{\rm inflaton}(\phi^{I},\partial\phi^{I})+\mathcal{L}_{\rm mod}(\psi,\partial\psi)+\dots\Big]\) |
| **Initial condition** | A regular (non‑singular) hypersurface or a well‑posed quantum state for the fields at a finite proper time \(t_{0}\). | \(a(t_{0})=a_{0}>0,\;\dot a(t_{0})>0,\;\phi^{I}(t_{0})=\phi^{I}_{0},\;\dot\phi^{I}(t_{0})=\dot\phi^{I}_{0}\) |
| **Consistency constraints** | (i) Einstein‑field‑equation (or its modified version) satisfaction, (ii) stability of perturbations, (iii) compatibility with observed limits on varying constants, (iv) algebraic‑QFT locality/causality if an AQFT description is adopted. | \(\displaystyle G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi G\,T_{\mu\nu},\qquad c_{s}^{2}>0,\qquad |\dot\alpha/\alpha|<10^{-17}{\rm yr^{-1}}\) (Uzan 2025) |

From the five records we can **derive** a minimal, modular framework that accommodates the most widely studied early‑universe mechanisms (single‑field inflation, multifield/non‑singular inflation, quintessential inflation, and dynamical‑constant scenarios) while remaining compatible with a rigorous algebraic‑QFT (Haag–Kastler) underpinning.

**D. Mathematical Framework and Assumptions**  

1. **Spacetime manifold**  
   - 4‑dimensional, globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold \((\mathcal{M},g_{\mu\nu})\).  
   - Metric signature \((-+++)\).  
   - Assumed spatial homogeneity and isotropy → Friedmann‑Lemaître‑Robertson‑Walker (FLRW) line element  
     \[
     ds^{2}=-dt^{2}+a^{2}(t)\,d\vec{x}^{2}.
     \]

2. **Field content**  
   - **Gravity**: Einstein–Hilbert term (or a modified gravity term, e.g. Gauss‑Bonnet).  
   - **Inflaton sector**: \(N\) scalar fields \(\phi^{I}(t,\vec{x})\) with a field‑space metric \(G_{IJ}(\phi)\).  
   - **Varying‑constant sector**: a scalar \(\psi(t,\vec{x})\) whose vacuum expectation value determines a dimensionless constant \(\alpha(\psi)\).  
   - **AQFT net**: a family of von‑Neumann algebras \(\{\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{O})\}\) indexed by open regions \(\mathcal{O}\subset\mathcal{M}\) satisfying isotony, locality, covariance, and existence of a vacuum state \(\Omega\) (Haag–Kastler axioms).
